minutes.headline: Sewer Commission chose Wright Pierce for preliminary sewer design; grease trap fee policy left unchanged for now.
minutes.summary: The commission heard the DPW director's report on four design proposals and moved to hire the low bidder. It then moved to accept the second quarter billing commitment and to send a letter on reviewing applicants for the assistant business manager post. A long grease trap policy and fee discussion ended without a change and will return to a later agenda. ARPA priorities, Fitchburg and Leominster invoices and FY22 budget status were also covered.

what_happened.line: The Sewer Commission moved to accept the DPW director's recommendation of Wright Pierce, the lowest of four bidders, for preliminary sewer design; the result was not audible.
The commission moved to accept the second quarter billing commitment; the result of the motion was not audible.
A motion was made to send a letter asking that assistant business manager applicants be forwarded to the business manager and DPW director for review.
A long grease trap policy and fee discussion ended with no decision and will return on a later agenda, after consulting the Board of Health chair and counsel.
The commission set a March 24 target for the finance committee budget date and agreed to put an ARPA wish list on the January agenda.

why_it_matters: The design contract is the first step toward sewer upgrades that ratepayers will eventually fund through sewer bills, and the grease trap fee, which a member said would lose the town revenue if dropped, is unsettled.
The ARPA wish list and the FY23 budget timeline show where federal money and next year's sewer budget will be decided, before the finance committee date.
watch_next: January Sewer Commission agenda: the ARPA wish list and the second-meeting budget discussion.
Finance committee budget date, targeted for March 24.

reconciliation.what: Our minutes against the minutes the town published. caption_error = the same fact the captions rendered badly, resolved by the official reading shown beside the as-heard one; discrepancy = a substantive difference, flagged and not resolved. Neither record is treated as the referee.
reconciliation.summary: The records agree on all three votes, the grease trap fees, the Q2 commitment amount, and the ARPA and January budget decisions; ours lacks the vote tallies. The main differences are the fourth design bid (75,000 vs $15,000), a $30,593 figure that ours attaches to FY22 budget status while the official minutes tie it to the delinquency transfer, and a different account of where the grease trap policy goes next.
